title: The town that couldn't stop dancing

lines.text: In 1518, people in one city started dancing, and could not stop.
It began in July, in Strasbourg, when a woman stepped into the street and danced for days.
Within days, more than thirty people had joined her.
By August, chronicles say somewhere between fifty and four hundred were dancing.
The city's solution? More music. They hired musicians and opened halls for the dancers.
Later accounts claim people danced until they died, but the city's own records don't mention any deaths.
Historians think it may have been mass psychogenic illness, fuelled by famine, disease and fear.
Five hundred years later, nobody knows exactly what happened.

sources.claim: Began July 1518 in Strasbourg with one woman (often named Frau Troffea); over thirty within days; 50 to 400 by August
Council hired musicians and opened guild halls, which backfired; contemporary city records don't mention deaths
Leading theory is mass psychogenic illness linked to famine, disease and hardship (John Waller)
